COMMERCIAL / ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE

Before a building becomes an opportunity.

By Max Fisher · Draft for review · 2026-10-29

This example demonstrates the structure of a commercial research brief. It describes no actual building, owner, contractor, or available project.

  • 1. The research questionIs this building worth a permission-based qualification conversation with an authorized representative?
  • 2. Public evidence to collectExact building ID, address, reporting period, energy observation, applicable target source, and checked date. Retain any conflicting records.
  • 3. What the record can establishA dated observation from a named source. A comparison is meaningful only when identity, units, reporting period, and target are compatible.
  • 4. What remains unknownCurrent decision authority, equipment condition, owner intent, project stage, approved scope, budget, procurement route, and timing.
  • 5. Contractor fit to verifyComparable projects, system expertise, commissioning capability, geographic coverage, and confirmed capacity.
  • 6. The next actionConfirm the owner’s need and permission, then decide whether a scoped technical assessment or an introduction is appropriate.

A record moves from research to a qualified opportunity when the missing pieces are confirmed. A public performance gap alone does not make that transition.

Illustrative structure only · No live lead, compliance determination, or project commitment.
